subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu text commands (/stop, /new, /status) no longer bypass queue during active agent run (3.8 regression)

question: Should Feishu whole-message text commands during active runs be limited to a safe local fast-path subset, or should stateful commands such as `/stop` and `/new` also become authorized text-slash turns that bypass the active-run queue?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but restoring every reported command changes command authorization and session-ordering semantics; automation should not pick that product and safety boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Choose Broad Command Policy First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the stateful-command boundary, then sponsor a focused Feishu/core fix with live proof.

options.title: Adopt Safe Local Subset
options.body: Only fast-path low-risk local commands such as `/status` and leave `/stop` or `/new` to a separate explicit design decision.

options.title: Restore All Reported Commands
options.body: Authorize and bypass `/status`, `/stop`, and `/new` with tests and live proof that ordering and access checks remain correct.

recommendation.title: Choose Broad Command Policy First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the stateful-command boundary, then sponsor a focused Feishu/core fix with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the shared command-gating and command-turn policy boundary points to this owner candidate.
